questions.question: NSK Chennai plant mainly makes bearings for which sector?
questions.explanation: The Chennai plant was set up to make automotive bearings such as hub units, transmission and magnetic clutch bearings.

questions.question: What is the first step of the 5S system?
questions.explanation: Seiri means sorting: remove everything not needed at the workplace before arranging what remains.

questions.question: Which Japanese word means continuous improvement?
questions.explanation: Kaizen means small, daily improvements made by everyone, from operator to plant head.

questions.question: Pulling the Andon cord signals what?
questions.explanation: An Andon alerts the leader to a quality or machine problem so it is fixed at once, not passed on.

questions.question: Bearing rings become hard in which process?
questions.explanation: Hardening and tempering give rings high hardness (about 58–64 HRC) needed for long rolling fatigue life.

questions.question: Which grinding finishes ring OD without centres?
questions.explanation: Centreless grinding supports the ring on a blade and regulating wheel, giving fast, accurate outer diameters.

questions.question: Superfinishing of raceways mainly improves what?
questions.explanation: Superfinishing removes fine grinding marks on raceways, lowering noise and helping form an oil film.

questions.question: Why are rings washed before assembly?
questions.explanation: Even tiny grinding particles left on rings cause noise and early failure, so rings are cleaned first.

questions.question: Gen-3 hub unit inner ring is clamped by what?
questions.explanation: Gen-3 hubs commonly use orbital (roll) forming of the hub end to clamp the inner ring and hold preload.

questions.question: Hub flange raceway is usually hardened by?
questions.explanation: Medium-carbon hub flanges are induction hardened only at the raceway, keeping a tough core.

questions.question: Poka-Yoke means what?
questions.explanation: Poka-Yoke devices stop wrong parts or wrong steps, so defects cannot be made or passed on.

questions.question: SMED is a method to reduce what?
questions.explanation: Single-Minute Exchange of Die moves setup steps outside machine stop time to cut changeover time.

questions.question: Minimum Cpk for a capable process?
questions.explanation: Automotive customers usually expect Cpk of at least 1.33, meaning the process stays well inside tolerance.

questions.question: X-bar R chart belongs to which tool?
questions.explanation: Statistical Process Control charts show when a process drifts so action is taken before defects occur.

questions.question: In PFMEA, RPN equals what?
questions.explanation: Risk Priority Number multiplies Severity, Occurrence and Detection; newer AIAG-VDA FMEA uses Action Priority.

questions.question: 4M change covers Man, Machine, Material and?
questions.explanation: Any change in Man, Machine, Material or Method must be planned, approved and verified before production.

questions.question: The fishbone diagram is also called?
questions.explanation: The Ishikawa (cause-and-effect) diagram groups possible causes of a problem by category.

questions.question: Pareto rule: 80% of problems come from?
questions.explanation: Pareto analysis ranks causes so the team fixes the vital few that create most defects.

questions.question: Gauge R&R study checks what?
questions.explanation: Gauge Repeatability & Reproducibility shows how much variation comes from the gauge and inspectors.

questions.question: Why-Why analysis asks 'why' how many times?
questions.explanation: Asking 'why' about five times digs past symptoms to the true root cause.

questions.question: LOTO must be applied before what?
questions.explanation: Lockout-Tagout isolates energy so the machine cannot start while someone works on it.

questions.question: TPM aims for zero what?
questions.explanation: Total Productive Maintenance targets zero breakdowns, zero defects and zero accidents.

questions.question: Jishu Hozen is maintenance done by whom?
questions.explanation: Autonomous maintenance means operators clean, inspect, lubricate and tighten their own machines daily.

questions.question: CLIT stands for Clean, Lubricate, Inspect and?
questions.explanation: CLIT is the daily autonomous maintenance routine that stops small issues becoming breakdowns.

questions.question: MTBF measures what?
questions.explanation: Mean Time Between Failures shows reliability; a higher MTBF means fewer breakdowns.

questions.question: MTTR measures what?
questions.explanation: Mean Time To Repair shows how fast the team restores a machine after a breakdown.

questions.question: Thermal imaging cameras detect what?
questions.explanation: Infrared thermography shows abnormal heat in motors, panels and bearings before they fail.

questions.question: Vibration analysis is which maintenance type?
questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance uses condition data like vibration to repair just before failure.

questions.question: Dressing a grinding wheel restores what?
questions.explanation: Dressing removes dull grains and loading, restoring cutting action and the wheel profile.

questions.question: Grinding spindle bearings fail early mostly due to?
questions.explanation: Dirt, coolant entry and poor lubrication cause most early spindle bearing failures.

questions.question: Which extinguisher suits electrical panel fires?
questions.explanation: CO2 does not conduct electricity and leaves no residue, so it is used on electrical fires.

questions.question: A Kanban card is a signal to?
questions.explanation: Kanban cards trigger production or movement only when the next process pulls parts.

questions.question: JIT stands for?
questions.explanation: Just In Time makes and moves only what is needed, when needed, in the amount needed.

questions.question: Takt time = available time ÷ what?
questions.explanation: Takt time sets the production pace to match customer demand.

questions.question: OEE = Availability × Performance × ?
questions.explanation: OEE combines uptime, speed and good-part rate into one measure of equipment effectiveness.

questions.question: Heijunka in production means what?
questions.explanation: Heijunka levels volume and product mix over time to avoid peaks and idle time.

questions.question: MRP calculates material needs from BOM and?
questions.explanation: MRP explodes the master schedule through the BOM, netting stock to plan material orders.

questions.question: WIP stands for?
questions.explanation: WIP is partly finished stock between processes; high WIP hides problems and blocks cash.

questions.question: The bottleneck process decides what?
questions.explanation: The slowest step limits total line output, so improvement starts at the bottleneck.

questions.question: Muda means what?
questions.explanation: Muda is any activity that adds cost but no value for the customer.

questions.question: PO stands for?
questions.explanation: A Purchase Order is the legal document to a supplier listing item, quantity, price and delivery.

questions.question: A GRN is made when?
questions.explanation: A Goods Receipt Note records material received at stores against the purchase order.

questions.question: Three-way match checks PO, GRN and?
questions.explanation: Payment is released only when the PO, received quantity and invoice all agree.

questions.question: Standard bearing ring steel grade is?
questions.explanation: SUJ2/100Cr6 high-carbon chromium steel is the standard bearing steel for rings and balls.

questions.question: RFQ stands for?
questions.explanation: A Request For Quotation asks suppliers for price and terms so buyers can compare offers fairly.

questions.question: Supplier PPAP must be approved before?
questions.explanation: Production Part Approval Process proves a supplier's part and process meet all requirements.

questions.question: Why buy one part from two suppliers?
questions.explanation: Dual sourcing protects supply if one vendor faces fire, strike or quality problems.

questions.question: Supplier rating tracks Quality, Delivery and?
questions.explanation: QCD ratings help buyers reward good suppliers and develop weak ones.

questions.question: Near rotating machines, never wear what?
questions.explanation: Loose clothes, jewellery and long hair can get caught in rotating spindles and shafts.

questions.question: Heat treatment quench oil tanks risk what?
questions.explanation: Hot quench oil can ignite; heat treatment areas need fire controls and trained operators.
